title: Effect of Shaker and Planetary Ball Milling on Graphite Structure: A Comparative Study
content: Graphene can be described as a two-dimensional carbonaceous nanomaterial composed of single-layer carbon atoms bound in a hexagonal honeycomb array of sp2-hybridized atoms. Since its isolation by peeling pyrolytic graphite with adhesive tape, it has gained research attention of the worldwide scientific community; due to its unique physical structure and superior electrical, thermal, optical, and mechanical properties which makes it highly valued for potential applications in the fields of biology, medicine, environmental science, electronics, energy, and materials science [1]. The main problem with the widespread use of graphene is that although there are adequate methods of obtaining it at the laboratory level for research applications, the techniques for large-scale production of graphene are scarce [2]
